name: SpeakEasy
tagline: Behavioral-interview practice that scores what you say and how you say it from video.
problem: Video interview analysis tools are sold to recruiters; applicants only meet them in the real interview and have no fair way to practice against that kind of scoring.
solution: Pick behavioral topics, answer generated questions on camera, and get verbal scores (relevance, STAR structure, insight, vocabulary, filler words) plus non-verbal scores (face, eyes, gestures, pauses, framing) with concrete pros and cons.
demo_moment: Record one answer and immediately see a breakdown of both your content and your body language.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Inverts a crowded enterprise market: the same analysis recruiters buy, pointed at the applicant.
Named a list of incumbents in the write-up, showing the team knew the market it was flipping.
Engineering discipline on LLM output: benchmarked providers, then added validation with automatic re-prompting until output met format rules.
Used a sponsor's model router as core infrastructure, fitting a sponsor prize lane alongside the main rubric.

lessons: Look for a tool that exists only for the powerful side of a transaction and build the other side's version.
